common_name: Chiquita Autumn Sage (Dwarf Red Salvia greggii)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in lean, well-drained to dry soil in full sun; its compact habit makes it well suited to small beds, rock gardens, and containers where larger greggii selections would sprawl.

directions: Chiquita is a dwarf Salvia greggii selection bred for a tidy, dense mound well under two feet tall, noticeably smaller than most autumn sage cultivars, yet it still produces the same abundant flush of true red, two-lipped flowers from spring through fall. Its small stature makes it a practical choice for edging, narrow beds, and mixed containers where standard-size greggii selections would quickly outgrow the space. Hummingbirds visit the flowers readily despite the plant's reduced scale. Shear lightly after each bloom flush and cut back by about a third in late winter to keep the compact form dense and floriferous; once established it tolerates heat and drought with minimal supplemental water.

common_name: San Antonio Rose Autumn Sage (Rose-Pink Salvia greggii)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained to dry, lean soil in full sun; this Texas-named selection is a dependable performer in Gulf Coast heat and humidity.

directions: San Antonio Rose is a Salvia greggii selection named for the vivid rose-pink of its two-lipped flowers, a shade clearer and brighter than the softer tones of 'Pink' or 'Pink Preference', borne in continuous flushes on a rounded, well-branched shrub from spring until hard frost. It is a steady draw for hummingbirds and native bees throughout the long Gulf Coast growing season and, like other greggii selections, thrives on lean, sharply drained soil with minimal irrigation once roots are established. Cut the whole plant back by a third to a half in late winter to renew dense, compact growth and maximize the coming season's bloom.

common_name: Peter Vernon Salvia (Deep Wine-Purple Greggii-Microphylla Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Peter Vernon is an English-raised Salvia x jamensis hybrid valued for deep wine-purple, almost claret-colored, two-lipped flowers held well above aromatic gray-green foliage on a compact, rounded shrub. It blooms in repeated flushes from late spring into fall, drawing hummingbirds and bees steadily through the long season, and its rich dark color reads well against the softer pinks and whites of other jamensis selections in mixed plantings. Like its greggii and microphylla parents it is highly drought-tolerant once established, needing little supplemental water on lean, sharply drained soil. Trim lightly after each bloom flush to keep growth dense and encourage continued flowering.
